questions.question: A tired driver:

options.text: Is usually more careful than other drivers.
May take longer to make important decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: May take longer to make important decisions.
questions.explanation: Tired drivers are slower to spot or react to dangers. Drowsy drivers cannot make important decisions as quickly as alert drivers.

questions.question: Do not smoke within ____ of a vehicle carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a vehicle carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: Which item is required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: All commercial trucks must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.question: ____ is required emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial trucks must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids, unless you need the engine running to operate a pump. Ground the tank before opening it and keep it grounded until after closing.

questions.question: If you feel tired before driving, you should:

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to get there quickly.

questions.explanation: Caffeine will not make you more alert. It may keep you awake, but your body needs real sleep. The only way to handle tiredness is to stop driving and get rest.

questions.question: Mirrors should be adjusted:

options.text: When you are standing next to the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Check mirrors before starting your trip. For vehicles with trailers, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: Identification numbers, shipping names, and hazard classes on shipping papers:

options.text: Should be shortened if using small paper.
Should be shortened to make them easier to read.
Should only be shortened if the abbreviation is easy to understand.

questions.explanation: Never shorten identification numbers, shipping names, or hazard classes on shipping papers. The only exception is if the regulations specifically allow the abbreviation.

questions.question: To avoid blocking traffic while driving a heavy vehicle, you should:

options.text: Try to pass other vehicles while driving uphill.
Ride the brakes while driving downhill.

questions.explanation: If your heavy vehicle cannot keep up with traffic speed, stay in the right lane when possible.

questions.question: When checking a mirror, you should:

options.text: Use only the driver's side mirror.

questions.explanation: Check mirrors with quick glances. If you look too long, you will travel a long distance without watching the road ahead.

questions.question: Why should you not use the trailer hand valve while driving?

options.text: It will disconnect from the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off the engine right away.
Do not use a fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine right away.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as soon as possible to stop the fire from spreading. Do not open the hood unless you must.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials, what should you do?

options.text: Have someone other than the driver do it.

questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials. Someone must always hold the nozzle and watch the fuel flow.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn or change lanes too quickly.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the parking brake.
Put the gearshift in first gear.

questions.explanation: Before checking the engine compartment, put on the parking brake and block the wheels. Check the engine before starting it.

questions.question: What do move over laws require?

options.text: Trucks to use the left lane.
All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
All vehicles to use the left lane.
All vehicles to move to the left lane if a flatbed trailer is in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights on is stopped on the side of the road, drivers must leave the lane next to it if they can do so safely. If you cannot move over, slow down and go with caution.

questions.question: When transporting radioactive materials, what is important to know?

options.text: Radiation will pass through to other packages.
The package should be placed in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.
The package should be made of wood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation will pass through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads from each radioactive package to all nearby packages. Rules limit how many packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: What must emergency response information include?
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must describe any immediate health hazards from the materials.

questions.question: What is true about distracted driving?

options.text: It only happens when you do something physical, like use a cell phone.
It can happen when your mind is distracted, like daydreaming.
It is okay on empty roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen when your mind is distracted, like daydreaming.
questions.explanation: Mental distractions are as dangerous as physical ones. You can look at a hazard but not see it if your mind is somewhere else.

questions.question: What are glad hands?
questions.explanation: Glad hands are coupling devices that connect the air lines from a tractor to a trailer with air brakes.
